Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family member has a new job and has shared some initial excitement about it with their relatives.
Situation2: They share only one open evening before a busy travel week.
Story: I stared at my phone, rereading the message from my daughter about her new job. She sounded so excited, and I knew she’d want to talk, to share every detail with me, her mom, her children’s grandma. I could already picture the family group chat lighting up, everyone chiming in, and I felt the familiar tug to be present, to keep our connection strong. But tonight was the only evening my boyfriend and I had together before he left for a week-long business trip. We’d planned a quiet dinner, just the two of us, something we both needed after days of missed calls and hurried texts. I could sense his anticipation, the way he’d been looking forward to this night, and I wanted to give him my full attention. My heart twisted as I weighed the expectations—my family counting on me to be there, my partner hoping for intimacy and focus. I sat on the edge of the bed, phone in hand, torn between two worlds, feeling the pressure build as I tried to decide who needed me more tonight.
